newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt erases gains, but still stuck in range.
newsitem.headline: German debt erases gains, but still stuck in range.

text.p: German debt erased session gains in quiet, late afternoon trading, but dealers were not yet worried these losses would be extended, saying instead the market was still largely stuck in a range at higher levels.
By 1540 GMT the March Bund futures contract, traded on Frankfurt's DTB, was down six basis points at 101.80 with the benchmark 2007 bond at 102.05 after Monday's 102.12 close.

Dealers said the market had run out of steam earlier this morning after breaking but not holding decisively above the resistance level of 101.92. Later softer U.S. Treasuries, which held steady after home sales data, also weighed on sentiment.

The U.S. reported home sales rose 13.3 percent to 756,000 units last year, marking the strongest rise since 1978. Several dealers said the news was potentially worrying as a continuing stream of strong economic data could move up the date when the Fed will be forced to raise interest rates.

Today's Fed meeting should offer no surprises, as most economists were still convinced the Fed does not yet see the need to curb inflationary pressures with an interest rate hike. The Bundesbank is also seen keeping rates steady on Thursday.
Bunds largely shrugged off this morning's German 1.4 percent rise in December industrial output.
And while the numbers seemed to point to stronger growth, economists said this was not accompanied by inflationary pressures which pleased the bond market.
Before official news on any Fed decision however, dealers said the market would likely trade in a range somewhere between 102 and 101.60.
Later this week a raft of German economic data, including orders and unemployment, is expected to provide new trading impulses.
